summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Crohn’s disease status post subtotal colectomy and ileorectal anastomosis was admitted for recurrent abdominal pain and severe watery diarrhea, with a concurrent left ankle injury. Initial evaluation revealed no bowel obstruction or fracture. Stool testing confirmed a C. difficile infection, likely contributing to his symptoms despite a history of recurrent episodes. He was treated with oral vancomycin, with significant improvement in abdominal pain and bowel frequency. His ankle pain resolved with conservative management. He was discharged home after four days on a full course of vancomycin and advised to follow up with gastroenterology to discuss fecal microbiota transplant due to recurrent C. diff.
